Onboarding

Try a local competition, step by step.

First check startup and scoring on one PC. For AWS hosting, review supported capabilities, costs and permissions in the organizer guide before configuring it separately.

01

Clone and start the host.

Follow the startup guide: clone, make install, then make local. Problems are acquired from selected URL/ref or local path sources. Keep the build enabled on the first start.

02

Create an event and a team.

Open 127.0.0.1:5174 on the host and sign in with the displayed organizer key. Create the event and team, select supported problems and start. Keep the organizer key private.

03

Join and check the score.

Join 127.0.0.1:5175 on the same PC with the team key. Try a native problem such as Crypto Battle and check actions and scores. See the startup guide for remote Tailscale access and Docker requirements.

Security

Your AWS account, still yours.

  • Cross-account AssumeRole + ExternalId. Operations use a registered role and verified ExternalId in the competitor account.
  • Verify ownership and cleanup. Check teardown results. Event data, retained storage and competitor bootstrap resources remain; review AWS billing as well.
  • The code is on GitHub. Inspect the Lambda functions, Step Functions and infrastructure code. Apache License 2.0.
  • Review usage and retained resources. The platform needs no always-running server, but API/database usage and retained storage are not guaranteed to cost zero.

Read the book

The whole method, in one book.

Build a local Challenge, an AWS Challenge, and an AWS Battle in increasing order of difficulty, then run them as a competition several teams can play. It is written around TenkaCloud, but reading it needs neither an AWS account nor a TenkaCloud install. Available in English and Japanese.

自分で作るクラウド競技 Japanese · Zenn Build Your Own Cloud Competition English · Leanpub
Commercial offerings

Three productized offerings — formally documented.

The OSS platform stays free under Apache 2.0. For organizations that want setup, live operations, or a program run for them, we offer three productized packages. Each has a fixed shape — scope, deliverables, exclusions, delivery model.

Hosted Event

One operated drill, end to end.

A 1-day cloud drill on the public OSS catalog, run by us. Event design, deploy into your AWS account, dry run, live facilitation, post-event report. Per-event fixed price.

Annual Arena

A 12-month program.

An annual contract of 4 operated events per year for one org: learning paths curated from the public problem catalog (beginner → advanced). Original problem development is not included in this package.

CCoE Enablement (add-on)

Advisory, sold separately.

A monthly retainer for operating-model / training-roadmap work. Never bundled into the two offerings above, so events stay productized. If you want both, that is two line items.

Pricing

Start small. Move to a yearly program.

The platform’s OSS license is free. AWS usage and retained storage can incur separate charges. Service fees for setup and event operations are listed below.

Future learning topics

Practice the human side of security.

An urgent request or a suspicious email. Pause, verify through another channel and choose a safe response. We are exploring exercises around these situations too.

TenkaCloud currently hosts hands-on cloud exercises. Social engineering exercises, including email judgment, are not yet available.
